The 10 best podcast apps for iPhone in 2026

November 2026

Podcast apps all play audio, so the differences are in the details: how new episodes reach you, how you control speed, what it costs, and who is watching. We looked at ten apps on the iPhone as of November 2026 and wrote down what each does best, and who should skip it.

Full disclosure: we make Margin. We've tried to be fair — every app here is good at something.

How we picked

We included apps that are live on the iPhone App Store today. Prices come from each company's own pages or its App Store listing, and may differ by country or change over time. We looked at:

  • Listening control: speed, queues and silence handling.
  • Staying on top of new episodes: how an app keeps a long list of shows manageable.
  • Cost and privacy: what is free, what is paid, and what an app says about tracking.

Quick picks

  • Best for controlling your listening and seeing your habits: Margin
  • Best for free and built in: Apple Podcasts
  • Best for faster, clearer listening: Overcast
  • Best for power features and playback everywhere: Pocket Casts
  • Best for sorting new episodes: Castro
  • Best for music and podcasts together: Spotify
  • Best for saving ideas: Snipd
  • Best for community and supporting creators: Fountain
  • Best for radio, audiobooks and podcasts: Castbox
  • Best for a one-time purchase: Downcast

1. Margin

Best for: Listeners who want control and clear stats on their own habits.
Price: Free to use. Margin Plus is optional: $1.99 a month or $19.99 a year in the US, with a 1-week free trial on the yearly plan.

Margin is ours, so weigh this entry accordingly. It is a podcast player for people who listen a lot: an Inbox for new episodes, more than one queue, chapters, and stats on where your listening time goes. Playing, following, downloads, the Inbox, Up Next, the sleep timer, CarPlay, widgets and iCloud sync are free; Plus adds things like transcripts, enhanced audio, custom skip times and per-show speed, Apple Watch playback and full stats. There is no account, no ads and no tracking, and you can export your shows and listening data any time. See Margin on the App Store.

Skip it if you want one app for music and podcasts, or you are not on an Apple device. Margin is for iPhone and iPad.

2. Apple Podcasts

Best for: Simple, free, built-in listening that syncs across Apple devices.
Price: Free.

Apple Podcasts is already on your phone, and it is better than its reputation. Its listing highlights editor-curated recommendations, Top Charts, Enhance Dialogue, transcripts you can read along with and share from, CarPlay, Apple Watch and widgets. It also handles subscriber-only shows from Apple and other apps.

Skip it if you want fine-grained control over speed and silence per show, or detailed listening stats.

3. Overcast

Best for: Smart Speed and Voice Boost in a clean, privacy-minded player.
Price: Free with ads that promote other podcasts. An optional annual Premium subscription hides them (check the App Store for the current price).

Overcast is written by a single developer and has been a favorite for years. Smart Speed shortens silences, Voice Boost evens out volume, and playlists with smart filters let you set per-show priorities. It has a standalone Apple Watch app and, per its listing, no third-party analytics, ad services or tracking code.

Skip it if you want transcripts or a more modern-feeling interface; its listing does not mention transcripts.

4. Pocket Casts

Best for: Power features and playback in more places, including Sonos and Chromecast.
Price: Free. Plus is $3.99 a month or $39.99 a year for new subscribers.

Pocket Casts offers playlists and smart playlists, trim silence, volume boost, speeds from 0.5x to 3x, chapters, and an Extra Dark theme for OLED screens. It also plays to CarPlay, AirPlay, Chromecast and Sonos, and syncs your Up Next queue when you sign in.

Skip it if you do not want to create an account to sync, or you would rather not pay yearly for the extras.

5. Castro

Best for: Triage: new episodes land in an Inbox and you pick what to queue.
Price: Free. Castro Plus is listed at $3.99 a month, $9.99 a quarter or $24.99 a year on the App Store, plus a $39.99 family plan.

Castro popularized the idea that subscribing to a show should not mean owing it every episode. New episodes arrive in an Inbox, you add the ones you want to your queue, and queued episodes download automatically. It also has CarPlay and an Apple Watch app.

Skip it if you like to hear everything a show publishes in order, where an inbox is just extra tapping.

6. Spotify

Best for: One app for music and podcasts, with a huge catalog.
Price: Free with ads. Premium Individual is $12.99 a month in the US, with offline downloads and other perks.

Spotify lists millions of podcast titles next to its music library, so one app covers both. If you already live in its playlists and recommendations, adding podcasts is easy, and you can follow free shows and build a library of them.

Skip it if you want to add shows from any RSS feed. Some shows exist only on Spotify, but a dedicated podcast player is built around open feeds.

7. Snipd

Best for: Capturing and revisiting key ideas from what you hear.
Price: Free, with AI features limited to 2 episodes a week. Premium is $6.99 a month, with a 1-week free trial.

Snipd is a podcast player built around saving highlights. Tap your headphones to save a moment as a snip, with an AI-generated transcript and summary, and sync to tools like Notion and Readwise. It also offers AI chapters, episode summaries and guest profiles.

Skip it if you just want to press play. Snipd is a knowledge tool first, and its AI features are where the free plan is limited.

8. Fountain

Best for: Community, clips and paying shows you love directly from the player.
Price: Free. The App Store lists an optional Fountain Premium purchase at $2.99.

Fountain mixes a player with a social layer: comments, shareable clips, playlists, and the ability to send a payment to a creator from the player. It still covers the basics, with a synced queue, chapters, searchable transcripts, per-show settings and OPML import from other apps.

Skip it if you want a quiet, solo listening app without feeds, social features or payments.

9. Castbox

Best for: Podcasts plus radio and audiobooks in a single app.
Price: Free. Castbox Premium is sold at several prices on the App Store, from about $3.99.

Castbox describes itself as over 95 million pieces of audio: podcasts, audiobooks, FM radio and sleep sounds. It supports Apple Watch and CarPlay and offers personalized recommendations, which suits people who like browsing.

Skip it if you prefer a focused podcast player. With this much in one app, podcasts are one section among several.

10. Downcast

Best for: A paid, no-subscription downloader with smart playlists.
Price: $2.99 on the App Store.

Downcast is a long-running app built around downloading: auto-download rules, episode retention settings, smart playlists, OPML import and export, iCloud sync and support for password-protected podcasts. It supports speeds up to 3x and chapters.

Skip it if you want frequent new features. The most recent update we could see on its App Store page was in January 2025.

How to choose

Start with what annoys you today. If new episodes pile up, try an inbox-style app like Castro or Margin. If you listen at high speed, compare Overcast, Pocket Casts and Margin. If you want it all in one place, Apple Podcasts or Spotify will do. Moving between apps is usually easy because most can import your shows by OPML, so a trial week costs you little.

FAQ

What is the best free podcast app for iPhone?

Apple Podcasts is free and already installed, and Overcast, Pocket Casts, Castro, Castbox and Fountain are free to download with optional paid upgrades. Margin is free to use too, with an optional Margin Plus subscription. Which one is best depends on whether you want built-in simplicity or extra control.

Which podcast app has the best features for fast listening?

Overcast offers Smart Speed and Voice Boost, Pocket Casts has trim silence and speeds from 0.5x to 3x, and Margin has per-show speed and skip settings with silence trimming. Check each app's listing, since some of these are in paid tiers.

Is there a podcast app with no account and no ads?

Margin has no sign-in, no ads and no analytics. Overcast is free with ads that promote other podcasts unless you subscribe to Premium.

Can I move my shows between podcast apps?

Usually yes. Most apps export and import an OPML file, which is a simple list of your subscriptions. Margin, Fountain and Downcast all list OPML import in their App Store descriptions.
